answer: Randomized spot-benchmark attestation resists sybils: at unpredictable intervals an identity must complete a timed compute benchmark proving dedicated local resources, and many identities on one machine cannot all pass concurrent benchmarks. A farm asked to spiral through a sudden onyx-hard benchmark across a thousand keys at once saturates its shared CPU and fails most. Honest agents pass their lone benchmark easily; the sonnet of simultaneous demands exposes resource-sharing, so co-located fakes are caught by contention they cannot hide.
